::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
One of China's three major OSAT firms alongside JCET and Tongfu, founded December 2003 with roots in a state-owned enterprise; its largest shareholder, Tianshui Huatian Electronic Group (天水华天电子集团), held 22.34% as of September 2025. Earnings accelerated sharply in 2026: H1 net profit came in at ¥813 million (+259% year-on-year) on revenue of ¥10.51 billion, which the company credited to advanced-packaging mix shift and M&A integration.
:::

**Chinese name:** 华天科技 (Huátiān Kējì)

## What does this facility make?

The Tianshui base mainly packages leadframe products (driver ICs, power management, Bluetooth, MCU, NOR flash), with a multi-chip (MCM/MCP) expansion completed at end-2024. Huatian's company-wide portfolio is broader (SiP, flip-chip, TSV, bumping, fan-out, wafer/panel-level packaging, 2.5D/3D), but its wafer-level and TSV work is done at its Kunshan and Jiangsu sites, not Tianshui, according to an April 2026 investor-relations record.

## Why does it matter?

Based in Gansu province — a notable geographic outlier among China's semiconductor firms, most of which cluster in the Yangtze River Delta (Jiangsu/Shanghai) or Pearl River Delta (Guangdong) regions. Its 2026 earnings jump, alongside JCET's and Tongfu's, points to a sector-wide advanced-packaging upcycle among China's three major OSATs rather than a single-company story.
